summary: GoHighLevel documents a broad REST API authenticated with OAuth 2.0 access tokens or scoped Private Integration Tokens at sub-account/location or agency level. Ongoing API access requires a paid HighLevel plan (14-day trial; Starter $97/month), and some endpoints require Founder eligibility. HighLevel operates remote Streamable HTTP MCP endpoints for supported AI clients; multi-sub-account agency use is rolling out and each request targets one authorized sub-account. Composio's preserved listing is the location-scoped HIGHLEVEL_LOCATION alias.
blocker: Useful access requires a paid HighLevel subscription, endpoint eligibility, scopes, and account permissions; restricted endpoints need a higher-tier plan. The preserved Composio alias is single-location, not agency-wide. MCP client/connector support does not mean HighLevel operates an MCP client, and bulk agency installation is not universally available.
next_action: Start with a HighLevel trial or paid account, create a least-privilege Private Integration Token for one location (or register a Marketplace OAuth app for user-authorized/agency use), verify endpoint plan eligibility, and test REST calls. For MCP, use the current client-specific HTTPS endpoint, approve only needed scopes/sub-accounts, and confirm bulk installation before agency-wide automation; use HIGHLEVEL_LOCATION only for one location.

auth.reason: Current official authorization and API pages document OAuth 2.0 and Private Integration Tokens, Bearer transport, and distinct sub-account versus agency credentials. The dated API page says legacy key generation is being phased out and V1 is end-of-support. Direct retrieval of the targeted Stoplight OAuth2/get-started routes still returned only Stoplight CSS/application shell and no readable HighLevel auth text; no sign-in was attempted, so substantive claims use the current HighLevel help and marketplace documentation.

official_mcp.reason: The 2026-11-15 official setup guide names the HighLevel/LeadConnector MCP Server, gives client-specific HTTPS endpoints, and requires OAuth consent. The undated marketplace reference explicitly describes remote Streamable HTTP servers and more than 700 actions. Supported clients consume HighLevel's server; Managed Agents' third-party MCP connectors are client behavior and were not substituted. The later 2026-11-15 guide says agency-wide connections are rolling out through bulk installation, while every request remains scoped to one authorized sub-account.

evidence.title: HighLevel MCP Server transport
evidence.quote: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard for connecting AI assistants to the apps you use. HighLevel uses it to connect compatible assistants that support remote Streamable HTTP servers and HighLevel’s sign-in flow.

evidence.title: HighLevel MCP Server authentication
evidence.quote: You connect by signing in with your HighLevel login, choosing your sub-account(s), and approving the requested permissions. There’s no key to create, paste, or rotate.

evidence.title: HighLevel MCP sub-account and agency scope
evidence.quote:
A single-sub-account connection is bound to the sub-account you choose during OAuth authorization for the lifetime of that connection.

Where agency-wide access is available, you can connect once and work across the sub-accounts selected during installation.

evidence.title: HighLevel MCP agency rollout limits
evidence.quote:
Every request targets one sub-account and is authorized against your installation. The connection cannot access sub-accounts you did not include.

Availability: Single-sub-account connections are available today. Agency-wide connections are rolling out through the multi-sub-account, or bulk, installation option. If installation offers only one sub-account, the multi-sub-account option is not enabled for your app yet.

evidence.title: HighLevel MCP operation coverage
evidence.quote: The table covers **717 supported actions across 38 feature areas**, grouped by the HighLevel menu. Available actions depend on your connection’s permissions and the features enabled in your sub-account.

verdict.reason: Broad REST coverage, modern OAuth/Private Integration Token authentication, and a HighLevel-operated remote MCP server support a gated build candidate. Ongoing use requires a paid HighLevel plan; endpoint eligibility, scopes, permissions, and the MCP bulk-install rollout constrain automation. Composio's preserved alias remains location-scoped. The pricing and marketplace reference pages are undated; the cited API/MCP support pages are dated 2026-11-15 and 2026-11-16.
